title: test_export_model_precommit fails accuracy validation for opt_gptq katuni4ka/opt-125m-gptq
signature: accuracy validation failed assertionerror in test export model precommit opt gptq katuni4ka|Code Issue

failed_jobs.name: PyTorch Models tests / PyTorch Models tests

key_errors: File test_llm.py:559, in compare_results: return super().compare_results([fw_outputs[0]], [ov_outputs[0]])
File test_convert_model.py:93, in compare_results: assert is_ok, 'Accuracy validation failed'
root_cause: The LLM export test for katuni4ka/opt-125m-gptq (GPTQ-quantized OPT model) fails because the exported OpenVINO model produces numerically different logits compared to the PyTorch reference outputs. This is an accuracy regression: during export_model_precommit the model is converted to an OV IR and then inferred on CPU, but the compare_results step asserts the first token outputs are close enough to the reference. The failure is deterministic (100% test completion before failure, not a timeout), suggesting a recent change in conversion logic, quantization handling, or numerical precision for GPTQ models broke parity. GPT-QModel 6.0.3 is being used with Torch 2.12.0+cpu.
recommended_actions: Identify the PR in the merge queue and review changes to OV PyTorch export/conversion for GPTQ models.
Run the failing test locally: pytest test_llm.py::TestLLMModel::test_export_model_precommit[CPU-opt_gptq-katuni4ka/opt-125m-gptq]
Check if the PyTorch frontend GPTQ/quantization conversion path was modified in the triggering PR (head SHA df90f62b89f315390dcf2ade49d2cf364fc45b63).
Compare fw_outputs[0] vs ov_outputs[0] to understand the magnitude of the accuracy divergence.
prevention_strategies: Add numerical tolerance checks for GPTQ-quantized model exports as a precommit gate. Ensure any changes to quantization conversion paths include regression tests with known-accuracy models.
historical_context: No previous identical pattern found in the database.
